title: A room in a shared flat
summary_es: Emma va a ver una habitación en un piso compartido: Ryan le enseña la casa y le explica el alquiler, los gastos y las normas.
prediction_prompt: Someone is looking for a room in a shared flat. What questions would you ask before moving in?

segments.speaker: ryan
segments.text: Hi, you must be Emma. Come in! I'm Ryan.

segments.speaker: emma
segments.text: Hi Ryan. Thanks for letting me see the room today.

segments.speaker: ryan
segments.text: No problem. So, this is the living room. We share it with two other people.

segments.speaker: emma
segments.text: It's bigger than I expected. Who else lives here?

segments.speaker: ryan
segments.text: There's Carla, who's a nurse, and Tom. He works from home, so he's here most of the day.

segments.speaker: emma
segments.text: Is it noisy during the week?

segments.speaker: ryan
segments.text: Not really. Carla works nights, so we try to be quiet in the mornings.

segments.speaker: emma
segments.text: That's fine. I'm usually out by eight anyway.

segments.speaker: ryan
segments.text: Great. And this is the room. It isn't as big as mine, but it gets a lot of light.

segments.speaker: emma
segments.text: Oh, I like it. Is the furniture included?

segments.speaker: ryan
segments.text: The bed and the desk are. You'd have to bring your own chair.

segments.speaker: emma
segments.text: OK. And how much is the rent?

segments.speaker: ryan
segments.text: It's four hundred and fifty a month, plus bills.

segments.speaker: emma
segments.text: How much are the bills, more or less?

segments.speaker: ryan
segments.text: About sixty each. That covers electricity, water and the internet.

segments.speaker: emma
segments.text: So just over five hundred in total. That's cheaper than my flat now.

segments.speaker: ryan
segments.text: There's also a deposit of one month's rent. You get it back when you leave.

segments.speaker: emma
segments.text: Of course. Are there any house rules?

segments.speaker: ryan
segments.text: Just a few. We take turns to clean the kitchen and bathroom every week.

segments.speaker: emma
segments.text: That sounds fair. And what about guests?

segments.speaker: ryan
segments.text: Friends can stay at the weekend, but we ask the others first.

segments.speaker: emma
segments.text: I'm happy with that. When is the room free?

segments.speaker: ryan
segments.text: From the first of next month. Two other people are coming to see it tomorrow, though.

segments.speaker: emma
segments.text: Then I'd better decide quickly. Can I tell you tonight?

segments.speaker: ryan
segments.text: Sure. Send me a message before ten and the room is yours.

connected_speech.phrase: It isn't as big as mine
connected_speech.explanation_es: Los dos *as* son débiles (/əz/): solo se oye bien *big*.

connected_speech.phrase: a deposit of one month's rent
connected_speech.explanation_es: *of* es débil (/əv/) y se une a *one*.
*I'd better* = *I had better* («más vale que…»). La *d* apenas se oye.
La *d* de *send* se funde con la *m* de *me*.

glossary.def_en: to use something together with other people
things like beds, tables and chairs
the money you pay every month to live in a place
what you pay for electricity, water, internet and so on
to include; to be enough to pay for something
money you pay at the start and get back when you leave
to do something one after the other
a person who comes to stay at your home
it is a good idea for me to do this now
